sources_note: The URLs in works[] are citations of somebody else's sequences, not places this build reaches: nothing in the game reads this file and no tool downloads from it. The corpus itself lives outside the repository, and the provenance is declared here as well as on each row.

study_set.description: Fan sequenced MIDI of Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance (Konami, 2002), measured only. Not committed, not copied, not used as generator input.

rules.name: diminished seventh as a passing colour
rules.test: A diminished seventh chord on any degree is accepted on a weak beat when both voices that form it move by step into and out of it, and the bass resolves down by semitone.
rules.because: The set spends 7 percent of its sonorities on dim7 and hdim7 chords, and 41 percent of its bass relative clashes are minor seconds or minor sevenths, which is the shape a diminished seventh makes against its own bass.
rules.fails: a dim7 that arrives by leap on a downbeat and leaves by leap reads as a wrong chord.

rules.name: chromatic approach to the tonic at a cadence
rules.test: A bass that arrives on the tonic from a semitone below or above is accepted when the upper voice holds a common tone or moves by step, and when the chromatic note is a whole beat or shorter.
rules.because: Chromatic notes are 10 to 42 percent of the notes measured, so a semitone bass arrival is the set's normal cadence colour and not an error.
rules.fails: a chromatic bass note longer than a beat under a chromatic upper voice, which is the m2 on a strong beat the gate already fails.

rules.name: tritone as an interval of the chord, not a clash
rules.test: A tritone between two voices is accepted when both pitch classes are members of the labelled chord (dim, aug, dim7, hdim7, dom7) and the chord is not on a strong beat with both voices leaping into it.
rules.because: A tritone is 22 percent of the measured bass relative clashes, so it is the commonest single colour in the set after the major second; the rule keeps it only where the chord explains it, which is what turns the interval into harmony.
rules.fails: a tritone between two voices in different chords, or one entered by leap on the downbeat.

rules.name: resolved appoggiatura on the strong beat
rules.test: A minor second or major seventh on a strong beat is accepted when it resolves by step within one eighth note and the resolving note is a chord member.
rules.because: 51 percent of the measured clashes sit on a strong or medium beat and 57 percent of the voices that make one resolve it by step, so the accent alone cannot be the test; the resolution window is.
rules.fails: an accented clash that is held for a beat or left by leap.

rules.name: organ doubling and octave parallel accepted inside a registration
rules.test: Parallel octaves between two voices are accepted when the doubling is constant for a whole phrase and the two voices keep the same interval for at least two bars, which reads as one part in two registers.
rules.because: The set's arrangements double the organ and string lines for whole sections; the arranger of a chip cue can do the same with a duty cycle pair.
rules.fails: a doubling that starts or stops inside a phrase, which draws attention to the parallel.

rules.name: strong beat clash allowed once per phrase at a cadence
rules.test: One unprepared clash per phrase is accepted on the beat before a cadence when the following chord is the tonic and the clashing voice moves by step.
rules.because: A single accented clash per phrase is what makes the set's cadences sound deliberate; it is the same budget the project already uses for risk 3 devices.
rules.fails: two such clashes inside four bars, which stops being a device and becomes the texture.

next: M1a decides which of these enter tools/counterpoint/rules.py. They are written as tests with a measured basis, not as permissions: every one of them narrows the existing fault.
